Here’s a **summary on LED (Light Emitting Diode):**

---

### 💡 **Working Principle**
- LED works on **electroluminescence** — it emits light when **current flows through it in forward direction**.  
- Inside, it has a **p-n junction diode**.  
- When electrons and holes recombine at the junction, **energy is released as light (photons)** instead of heat.

---

### ⚙️ **Structure**
- **Semiconductor material:** Usually **Gallium, Arsenic, Phosphorus, Nitrogen** combinations.  
- **Anode (+)** = longer leg → connected to positive.  
- **Cathode (−)** = shorter leg → connected to negative.

---

### 🎨 **Colors & Materials**
| Color | Material Used | Approx. Wavelength |
|--------|----------------|--------------------|
| Red | Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) | 620–750 nm |
| Green | Gallium Phosphide (GaP) | 520–570 nm |
| Blue | Gallium Nitride (GaN) | 450–495 nm |
| White | Combination of RGB or Blue LED + Phosphor | — |

---

### ⚡ **Key Characteristics**
- Works at **low voltage (≈2–3V)**  
- **High efficiency**, **low power** consumption  
- **No filament**, so **long lifespan**  
- **Instant ON/OFF** response  
- **Direction-sensitive** (only works in forward bias)

---

### 🔋 **Typical Applications**
- Indicators (TV, chargers, etc.)  
- Display boards  
- Street & home lighting  
- Optical communication  
- Remote controls, sensors, etc.
